#### 1. autosomal dominant striatal neurodegeneration type 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.663)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:8794)

**Proposed mechanism:** Phosphodiesterase 8B (HGNC:8794) —DISRUPTS→ PDE8B activity (GO:0004049); PDE8B activity (GO:0004049) —DECREASES→ cyclic AMP (CHEBI:17475); cyclic AMP (CHEBI:17475) —INCREASES→ Striatal neuron function (GO:0007274); Striatal neuron function (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration of striatum (HP:0002314); Striatal neuron function (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal dysfunction (HP:0011257). Loss-of-function mutations in PDE8B lead to decreased hydrolysis of cAMP, resulting in elevated cAMP levels. This dysregulates normal striatal neuron function, ultimately causing neurodegeneration and neuronal dysfunction characteristic of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PDE8B with a clear gain-of-function mechanism for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs142988263)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PDE8B and cAMP signaling in striatal neurodegeneration could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting phosphodiesterase activity or cAMP levels for both MONDO:0013616 and autosomal dominant striatal neurodegeneration type 1.
